name: EchoStar Corporation
sector: Telecommunications / Pay-TV, wireless and satellite broadband
moat_justification: The scarce licensed spectrum was the one genuinely defensible asset, and it is being sold; what remains is a melting pay-TV base, a subscale wireless brand that no longer owns its network path, and a satellite-broadband business losing subscribers to Starlink. Subscriber inertia and a spectrum-sale payday are real, but there is no durable pricing power or switching-cost moat in the operating businesses — weak, 3/10.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 2.2%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT: a >60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs — check for divestitures, big M&A, or restatements before trusting any CAGR
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
one_liner: Melting pay-TV/wireless operator, moat 3/10, whose value sits in spectrum-sale proceeds rather than owner's earnings — conservative OE is negative on the median (-$2.66/share), latest-FY (-$3.83/share) and TTM (-$2.19/share) bases, so Tier F on this screen and no 15%-clearing price is computable from an OE DCF.
moat_for: Remaining licensed spectrum is a scarce regulator-created asset strategics paid tens of billions to acquire
Installed subscriber inertia: 6.39M pay-TV and 7.38M wireless subscribers at Q2 2026
Boost survives as a hybrid MVNO on AT&T with a Starlink Direct-to-Cell agreement attached to the SpaceX deal
moat_against: Pay-TV in secular decline with no pricing power against streaming
Retail wireless subscale vs the three national carriers and now dependent on AT&T wholesale network after the 5G build was abandoned
Hughes broadband losing subscribers against Starlink scale
Distressed capital structure: going-concern warning and DISH DBS Chapter 11 hand bargaining power to creditors
